Hi Samir / Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side focused on the performance items you flagged: latency SLOs, throughput/concurrency, and streaming support for real-time scoring.

Key items I captured:
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for 8k-context chat requests (streaming enabled)
- Peak throughput: ~6000 tokens/sec sustained during batch jobs; occasional spikes to 12k tokens/sec for nightly processing
- Concurrent active sessions: up to 45 simultaneous streaming connections during peak business hours
- Model family: primarily 70B transformer variants. You mentioned potential interest in LLaMA- or Mistral-family tuned checkpoints.

Requested next steps:
1) We'll run a short dedicated-capacity sizing/validation plan comparing GPU types (A100 vs H100) with your workload profile.
2) Please share a small representative prompt set (5–10 requests) and expected token distributions so we can mirror latency/streaming behavior.
3) We'll propose a reserved throughput number (tokens/sec) and an initial node count for a Dedicated pool and share benchmark artifacts.

Attaching an initial sizing doc and our benchmarking template (stub) — we’ll fill in results after the validation run.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the targets look right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The p95 <= 150ms is critical for our chat product; p99 can be relaxed to <= 500ms in non-peak windows.
- For nightly batch scoring we care more about tokens/sec (throughput) than per-request latency, but would like the pool to handle both without impacting the chat SLOs.
- We use streaming over websockets for chat; low first-byte latency matters for perceived responsiveness.

I'll attach a short prompt set and a token distribution CSV — sending separately via SFTP (security team restriction).

One ask: can your validation report include both A100 and H100 runs with identical config (sequence lengths, batching) so we can compare unit economics?

Appreciate it — Samir

Marissa / team / Samir —

Below is a proposed validation plan and early sizing guidance based on similar 70B workloads we've run:

1) Test matrix (A100 vs H100):
   - Model: 70B LM (fp16 baseline), sequence lengths: 2048 (batch) and 8192 (streaming chat)
   - Batch config: continuous batching targeting throughput stabilization; target sustained 6k tokens/sec
   - Streaming config: greedy sampling with kv-cache and network emulation to match websocket RTT

2) Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency (first-byte and completion), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, and end-to-end websocket connection concurrency impact.

3) Early findings from internal runs (approximate):
   - A100 (80GB) node: handles ~2.2k tokens/sec per GPU for 8k-context streaming at p95 ~160–200ms (depends on batch packing). Concurrency of ~10–12 streams per GPU before p95 degrades past 200ms.
   - H100 (80GB) node: ~3.5k tokens/sec per GPU for same workload, p95 ~110–150ms, concurrency of ~18–20 streams per GPU.
   - Note: These are ballpark numbers; exacts depend on model architecture, tokenizer behavior, and compilation knobs. Quantized int8 runs can improve throughput ~15–30% with some accuracy delta.

4) Recommended reserved throughput & sizing (initial commit):
   - If the SLO is strict p95 <=150ms for 8k streaming and you need 45 concurrent streams: recommend an H100 pool with 3–4 GPUs (estimate 18 streams/GPU -> 3 GPUs covers 54 streams headroom) and reserved throughput of 12k tokens/sec.
   - If cost-sensitive and willing to accept slightly higher p95, A100 pool with 6 GPUs (2.2k tokens/sec * 6 ≈ 13.2k tokens/sec) could be an option but will have less headroom for concurrency spikes; recommend autoscale/burst for short spikes.

5) Validation timeline & artifacts:
   - We can run the A100 vs H100 test matrix in ~48 hours once we have the prompt set and representative token distribution and can provision a small Dedicated pool.
   - Deliverables: raw benchmark CSV (attached), summarized latency/throughput deck, and final sizing recommendation.

Action items: Samir to confirm prompt set upload ETA; Marissa to confirm whether Arcadia prefers H100 cost baseline or A100 conservative baseline for procurement.

I'll start the baseline runs once we get the artifacts.

-Aditya
Principal Engineer, Inference Performance | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Samir
